title: Guttering, Ramps & Drainpipes
strapline: Join the pipes, tip in the water, and chase the flow across the whole garden.
intent: Children build channels and ramps and investigate how water and balls flow, exploring gradient, speed and direction.
Children plan, connect and adjust a system, solving real engineering problems as they go.
Children experience early physics — slope, flow, fast and slow, uphill and downhill — through hands-on play.
Children collaborate to build and run a long track that no one child could manage alone.
Children develop the language of movement and gradient — pour, flow, steep, gentle, faster, downhill, connect.
implementation: Provide lengths of guttering, drainpipe, tubing and funnels, plus balls, water and things that roll.
Offer fences, crates, tyres and blocks to prop the channels at different heights and angles.
Let children build and test freely: connect the pieces, tip in water or a ball, and watch what happens.
Model the investigating question: 'what makes it go faster — a steep slope or a gentle one?'
Feed in gradient and flow language as children play — steeper, slower, downhill, connect, join, gap.
Encourage joining channels into a long run, which naturally needs teamwork and planning.
Extend with a target at the end — a bucket to hit, a wheel to turn — so the flow has a purpose.
key_questions: What makes the water go faster?
How can you join the pipes so there's no gap?
Which way will the ball roll — uphill or downhill?
How could you get the water to reach the bucket?
What happens if you make the ramp steeper?

impact.text: Children build channels and ramps and test how things flow.
Children investigate slope, speed and direction.
Children connect and adjust a system to solve problems.
Children collaborate to build and run a long track.
Children use the language of gradient and flow.
Children persist to make water or a ball reach the target.

enhancements: A water source — butt, jugs or a pump — to keep the flow going.
Balls, marbles and things that roll to compare with water.
A wheel or waterwheel at the end for the flow to turn.
Crates and blocks at graded heights to change the gradient.
A bucket target to aim the flow into.
Corks and boats to float down the longest channel.

playing_exploring: Children explore how water and balls move through the channels.
They test different slopes, joins and heights.
active_learning: Children persist to close the gaps and make the flow reach the end.
They work together on a long, shared run.
creating_thinking: Children predict how slope changes speed, then test it.
They plan and adjust the system to solve flow problems.
